newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Computer makers see business booming in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Computer makers see business booming in Argentina.

text.p: Major computer makers see business growing this year and next in Argentina mostly due to economic reforms, but they say access to credit is restrictive.
In a poll of the industry published Tuesday by the daily El Cronista, Hewlett Packard said it expects sales to pick up 50 percent this year and 35 percent in 1997.

Acer sees business growing 45 percent this year and 18 percent next. Compaq expects sales to rise 30 percent in 1997 and International Business Machines Corp 12 percent. Compaq and IBM did not provide 1996 data.
Hewlett Packard said its payroll increased by 35 percent this year and Compaq by 20 percent. Acer also reported hiring more employees, while IBM said its payroll remained the same.

In general, computer makers said the free market changes undertaken by the government five years ago were helping their industries, but they complained that their clients found it hard to access credit to purchase their products.
Tomas Franke, head of Compaq Argentina, also complained about a recent, steep rise in fuel prices. "We felt forced to absorb the extra cost," he said.

Acer's head Fernando Portela welcomed a recent crackdown on smuggling. "This will let us access to a large portion of the market of PCs and peripherals, 50 percent of which was dominated by contraband," he said.
But Portela said the overall legal framework should be propped up in order to improve the business atmosphere.

Hewlett Packard Argentina's Hugo Strachan said his firm expected sales to rise by 35 percent in 1997. "We have confidence in this figure because it goes along with the structural changes under way in Argentina," he said.

Wilmer Guecaimburu, president of IBM Argentina, which was hit by a series of court scandals including alleged bribes and the cancellation of a $250 million deal with the state-owned Banco Nacion earlier this year, said sales to the private sector were helping make up for those setbacks.

"IBM Argentina has always done more business with the private sector than with the state. This has helped us overcome adequately the drop in business with the state sector, although we have also closed several deals with public agencies," Guecaimburu said.
